title: A Father’s Promise
content:
Siddu looked down for a moment before continuing.

"After leaving the college, every step toward home felt heavier than the last. Countless thoughts raced through my mind, and each one frightened me more than the previous."

"I was certain my father would be furious."

"I imagined him shouting at me..."

"Questioning every decision I had made..."

"Maybe even losing his trust in me."

He smiled faintly.

"But what actually happened..."

"...was something I never expected."

Sneha listened quietly.

"As soon as I reached home, I slowly pushed open the front door."

"I stepped inside..."

"...and everything was normal."

"There was no shouting."

"No anger."

"No disappointment."

"I was completely confused."

Siddu looked at the floor as though reliving that evening.

"My father walked toward me."

"He gently took my bag from my shoulder."

Then, in his usual calm voice, he said,

"Go and sit."

"I quietly sat on the chair."

"For a few moments..."

"...neither of us spoke."

"The silence itself made me nervous."

Then my father finally looked at me and asked,

"Siddu... tell me honestly."

He paused.

"Do you love a girl in your college?"

"My heart skipped a beat."

"Fear took over before honesty could. My first instinct was to deny everything."

"No, Dad."

"My father looked into my eyes."

For a moment...

"He simply smiled."

Then he said something that completely changed the way I looked at him.

"Listen carefully."

"Falling in love at your age isn't wrong."

"But sacrificing your future because of love is."

"If you truly love someone..."

"First build your own life."

"Become someone who can protect that love, not just with emotions, but with responsibility."

"Then come to me."

"If your feelings are still the same..."

"I will never stand in your way."

"The room became silent."

Sneha's eyes slowly widened.

Siddu smiled softly.

"I couldn't believe what I had just heard."

"I had prepared myself for punishment..."

"But instead..."

"...I found understanding."

"My father asked me once again."

"Now tell me honestly."

"Is that girl... Shreya?"

Siddu lowered his head.

"At that moment..."

"I realized I couldn't lie to him anymore."

"If I lied even then..."

"I would only be lying to myself."

"So, I looked into his eyes and answered honestly."

"Yes, Dad."

"I love Shreya."

"And she loves me too."

"My father remained silent for a few seconds."

Then he asked,

"So... what are you going to do now?"

"I didn't need time to think."

"I already knew my answer."

"Dad..."

"I'll focus on my studies."

"I'll crack JEE."

"I'll build my career first."

"If my feelings for Shreya remain the same after that..."

"Then I'll go back and ask her again."

A warm smile appeared on my father's face.

He slowly nodded.

"If you truly stand by those words..."

"Then I'll stand by you."

"For the first time that entire day..."

"The tears I had been holding back finally escaped."

"The tears I had been holding back since the principal's office finally broke free."

"I walked straight to my father..."

"...and hugged him tightly."

"I love you, Dad."

"Thank you..."

"Thank you for trusting me."

My father gently wiped the tears from my face.

He kissed my forehead.

Then, softly patting my back, he smiled and said,

"Enough..."

"Don't cry anymore."

"Your future is still in your hands."

Siddu looked at Sneha with a peaceful smile.

"That day..."

"I realized something."

"Sometimes..."

"The person who understands your heart the most..."

"...isn't your best friend."

"...isn't the person you love."

"It's your father."

"That day, I didn't just gain my father's support... I gained the strength to stand back up."
